clue.text: Rascal attached to one fish

parts.note: a scamp is a mischievous rascal
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A rogue is somehow tied to a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampi are Dublin Bay prawns, a shellfish served battered, so loosely a fish dish.

clue.text: There could be a catch in it

definitions.text: There could be a catch in it

parts.words: There could be a catch in it
parts.note: reads like a warning of a hidden snag, but means a basket an angler keeps the fish he has caught in

explanation.definitionFit: An angler's wicker basket holds the day's haul of fish.

clue.text: Criminal intended to limit one's credit

indicators.note: to limit means to hem in, so the word for intended encloses the other pieces

parts.note: meant is a synonym of intended
one is I, and the possessive 's gives IS
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: A crook meant to cap how much one could borrow.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscreant is a wrongdoer or villain.

clue.text: On the slope, girl loses her footing at the bottom of it

indicators.note: in a down answer the trimmed name goes underneath the other word

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down entry her footing is her last letter, which the girl's name drops

parts.note: Alice is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl on a slippery incline loses her footing at the foot of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loses her footing' trims ALICE to ALIC; 'at the bottom of' places that below IT in the down grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Italic type slopes to the right, so it is lettering set at a slant.

clue.text: Realised error involving the stars

indicators.note: an error means the letters of the clue word go wrong and come out rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone saw their mistake in reading the stars.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidereal describes what relates to or is measured by the stars, as in sidereal time.

clue.text: The 23rd seed going astray, badly

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters of the phrase before it are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A gardener's seeds blow off course and do poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges SEED GOING ASTRAY. England's patron saint has his feast on 23 April.
explanation.definitionFit: The feast of England's patron saint falls on 23 April each year.

clue.text: Shop with little room and little weight

parts.note: a den is a small private room
an ounce is a small imperial unit of weight

explanation.surface: A store with a tiny floor area and light stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shop' is the verb: to inform on someone, British slang for betraying them to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: To shop someone in British slang is to inform against them, to condemn them publicly.

clue.text: Flower I have planted between two more

indicators.note: planted between means set in the middle of the two letters that flank it

parts.note: two more flowers, ie ..., each abbreviated R on maps
contracted to I've

explanation.surface: A gardener puts one bloom between two others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' means something that flows; 'two more' of them are two rivers, each R.
explanation.definitionFit: A flower in crosswords is something that flows, such as a stream.

clue.text: Raphael, for instance, in fresh clothes breaking Charles's heart

indicators.note: breaking means splitting the central letters open to admit the other piece
the heart means the central letters of the name are used

parts.note: a change is a fresh set of clothes

explanation.surface: A heavenly messenger in new garments wins Charles's affections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' takes the central three letters of the name, and 'breaking' means the fresh clothes split them open; 'Raphael' leads the eye towards the painter rather than the archangel.
explanation.definitionFit: Raphael is one of the chief angels named in scripture and tradition.

clue.text: A novel religious sect

definitions.meaning: a book by Jane Austen, her last completed one
a denomination or body of believers

explanation.definitionFit: It is the title of Austen's final finished book, and also a word for a body of believers sharing one faith.

clue.text: Several diamonds show a blemish

parts.note: V, the Roman numeral five, stands loosely for several
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A cluster of gems has a visible flaw.
explanation.definitionFit: A vice is a moral failing or flaw in character.

clue.text: What Ko-Ko had about a jolly scaremonger

indicators.note: about means going round, so the Mikado phrase encloses the others

parts.note: Ko-Ko in Gilbert and Sullivan's Mikado sings 'I've got a little list'
a jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM

explanation.surface: Ko-Ko's possession concerns a cheerful doom-monger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A and RM inside A LIST.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarmist spreads needless fear, a panic-raiser.

clue.text: Neural disorder is imaginary

indicators.note: disorder signals that the letters of the clue word are jumbled

explanation.surface: A nervous-system condition turns out to be all in the mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Unreal and imaginary are synonyms for something not existing in fact.

clue.text: Nuts — crack almond to start with

parts.note: a crack is a joke, as is a gag

indicators.note: to start with takes the opening letter of the word for the nut

explanation.surface: A recipe: crack the almond first.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaga and nuts are both slang for crazy.

clue.text: All together make amends to Father in person

parts.note: to atone is to make amends
Father Time is time personified

explanation.surface: Everyone united to make peace with a priest face to face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father in person' is Father Time, the personification of time.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means simultaneously, everything happening on one occasion.

clue.text: Trade using former coins

parts.note: ex means former
change is loose coins

explanation.surface: Dealing in money that is no longer legal tender.
explanation.definitionFit: To exchange is to swap or barter goods.

clue.text: Deluge can have left: a complication

indicators.note: a complication means the letters are tangled up into a new order

explanation.surface: A flood may leave behind a tricky problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complication' rearranges CAN HAVE, L and A.
explanation.definitionFit: An avalanche is an overwhelming flood, literally of snow or figuratively of anything.

clue.text: Disposal of property not subject to tax — it's voluntary

parts.note: tax-free goods are free
a will disposes of a person's property after death

explanation.surface: A bequest that escapes duty is given willingly.
explanation.definitionFit: A free-will offering is one given by choice, unforced.

clue.text: One with intent, perhaps, to err and lie abominably

indicators.note: abominably means the letters are treated terribly, ending up shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone who means to make mistakes and lie dreadfully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abominably' rearranges TO ERR and LIE. Loitering with intent was a British offence of hanging about planning a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Under old British law a person lingering with intent to commit a crime could be charged.

clue.text: Efficient as third man, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the name is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: after Adam and Cain, Abel was the third man in Genesis

explanation.surface: A competent player fills the cricket position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Third man' looks like the cricket fielding position, but it means Abel, the third man in the Bible after Adam and Cain.
explanation.definitionFit: Able means capable and competent at a task.

clue.text: Fit army up with gear

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the army's letters read bottom to top

parts.note: the TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
tack is a horse's harness and gear

explanation.surface: Equip soldiers with kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TA into AT in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fit and an attack both name a sudden bout of illness, as of coughing.

clue.text: A shilling and some copper in payment for grass

indicators.note: in means set inside the word for the payment

parts.note: a fee is a payment
S was the abbreviation for a shilling in old British money
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Someone is paid in small change for some turf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container. A shilling was a pre-1971 British coin, abbreviated S, and 'some copper' points to the chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Fescue is a genus of grasses used for lawns and pasture.

clue.text: Little bit of French vineyard given to doctor

parts.note: a cru is a French vineyard or its growth
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A small share of a French wine estate goes to a physician.
explanation.definitionFit: A crumb is a tiny fragment, a morsel.

clue.text: Charm obtained by 'Open sesame'

definitions.meaning: to charm is to enchant or delight
the magic words in Ali Baba let the speaker into the cave

explanation.definitionFit: To enrapture someone is to enchant them; Ali Baba's magic words gave access through the cave door.

clue.text: Produce the effect of bird-song, soundwise

indicators.note: soundwise means taken by how the word is spoken

parts.note: caws are the calls of crows and rooks

explanation.surface: Birdsong has an audible effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the effect of' is link material leading from the verb to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To cause something is to bring it about or generate it.

clue.text: The place to tell stories, you said .

parts.note: to tell stories is to fib, to lie

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the word becomes the letter it sounds like

parts.note: taken as the spoken word

explanation.surface: Where yarns get spun, you say.
explanation.definitionFit: Lieu means place, as in 'in lieu of' meaning in place of.

clue.text: Brave group used to exercise

parts.note: a brave is a Native American warrior, an old use of Indian
a club is a group or society

explanation.surface: A team of warriors puts in some training.
explanation.walkthrough: Indian clubs are bottle-shaped wooden clubs swung in gym exercises.
explanation.definitionFit: These bottle-shaped wooden clubs are swung for gymnastic training.

clue.text: Shot into the light, so to speak

indicators.note: into means put inside the name of the flare

parts.note: a Very (or Verey) light is a signal flare
shot means cannon balls

explanation.surface: Something fired into the glare, as it were.
explanation.walkthrough: A Very light is a coloured flare fired from a pistol, named after its inventor; 'Shot' means ammunition, not a photograph or attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbally means in words, by speech rather than writing.

clue.text: Locking device we hear for each warder

indicators.note: we hear means the word is taken as spoken, spelt another way

parts.note: a key works a lock
per means for each

explanation.surface: A prison officer's lock gadget for everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: A keeper and a warder both guard prisoners.
